title: Recreating Toxic Mobile Games for My Kid
author: ScaleInfamous1847
selftext:
I've been coding for years but only recently started using AI for game development (was pretty sceptical, I enjoy writing code and it felt like a cop out, but I've ended up really liking the process of directing the project instead of typing everything by hand).

I've been aiming to remake the kinds of games my daughter enjoys playing, but without the endless ads and in-app purchases. Latest project is a nut & bolt sorting game if anyone fancies taking a look: [https://snug-e1be7.web.app/](https://snug-e1be7.web.app/)

I'd love any feedback, especially from people who've gone down a similar AI-assisted development rabbit hole.

comments.author: AceHighness
comments.body: I tried it out ... looks fun for kids. i'm not a kid, but there you go. The world needs more free games without ads.

replies.author: shimroot
replies.body:
I kinda agree with that and don’t. People making games should have a way to support themselves. 

On the other hand the ads most of these game shove down your throat make me want to see the world burn.

So there’s that.

replies.author: AceHighness
replies.body: Sure, but if your game is not worth buying and you have to push ads in there, it's probably not that good. Do we really have to feel bad if that earning model finally collapses? Anyone can make their own match 3 game instead of playing candy crush. I don't think that's a bad thing and neither is putting them out there for free. i have \~40 free games online with 0 ads.

replies.author: shimroot
replies.body: Oh wow. Can you share them? I’m curious what games you made 😃

replies.author: AceHighness
replies.body:
sure they are all over at [www.vibegamesstudio.com](http://www.vibegamesstudio.com)

new ones get added, and the current ones keep getting improved. let me know which ones you liked!

replies.author: ScaleInfamous1847
replies.body:
Absolutely agree and a few ads here and there are no bother - or a small fee (I'd prefer that) but the one I based this on was like 3 seconds of gameplay for 30 seconds of ad and all the hints and undos were behind a paywall.

That sort of thing isn't some small developer with a neat idea, it's a huge app farm taking advantage.

replies.author: shimroot
replies.body: Yeah, I agree. Encountered those myself, it was an instant uninstall when I saw that.

replies.author: Gh0st3d
replies.body: I've always wondered if I bypassed ads but just made users wait 30s with a screen that says something along the lines of "I don't want to run ads, but if you hate waiting, pay to remove this interruption" would people be more inclined to pay haha

replies.author: shimroot
replies.body: Oh that’s a nice idea to test out. It’s probably closer to what Spotify was doing? Their ads were promoting paid Spotify

replies.author: ScaleInfamous1847
replies.body:
That's a really solid idea though. Charge a few quid to get rid of it but just have a countdown with - sorry this sucks, but it sucks less than an ad!?

£1 to remove.

Wouldn't make you a millionaire but for a good fun game I reckon you'd do ok.

From a parents perspective I'd be chucking £1 all over the place to stop my kid from watching those bloody INSERT WORD HERE-scape ads

replies.author: Lower-Hedgehog-9835
replies.body: Have it score by moves v minimum moves

replies.author: ScaleInfamous1847
replies.body:
It kinda does, you get a flawless win if you complete using the minimum possible without any hints or undos.

You get 3 gold for doing it within target but there's always that extra flawless if you want to aim for it.

replies.author: Lower-Hedgehog-9835
replies.body: Make it more explicit. Im a phd in cog testing. Trust me. Even if you have it in the background. Its the best metric of difficulty / capacity for this task

replies.author: ScaleInfamous1847
replies.body: Yep, done! Has a league table for each level of moves and times. Great suggestion!

replies.author: Runesun
replies.body: They are recreating the games that are toxic and filled with ads from mobile stores with a non-toxic ad-free version so his kid avoids all that. Title confused me too. Lol

replies.author: Ok-Investment4414
replies.body: oh lol yeah i was like wtf so the experience is toxic lol ngl really those games piss me off even dangling nice options behind an ad that is 5 minutes long with a hidden X button.

replies.author: everyoneLikesPizza
replies.body: Ads and in app purchases

comments.author: everyoneLikesPizza
comments.body: If you finish the game you could sell it on the App Store for 2.99 with “NO ADS OR IN APP PURCHASES, COMPLETE PRODUCT” as a selling feature

replies.author: ScaleInfamous1847
replies.body: Nah, this is just for fun and to see what's possible. It's much more me than I thought it would be, but it's still AI doing the hard work.

comments.author: Ok-Constant-8319
comments.body:
Love it. I did some similar games for the same reason. Endless runner Minecraft's game at https://craftrush.royashbrook.com and a kind of roll around Katamari style game at https://quantamari.royashbrook.com. Both on  github and meant to be PWA installed so you can play offline. Not perfect.

I am currently targeting one of those resource games where you make pizzas or gather gold or whatever. Same reason. Kids want to play them and they seem to only be in super ad pumped up games. 

Sorting game is great!

replies.author: ScaleInfamous1847
replies.body: They are so good! I'll get my kiddo on the Minecraft one, she's seen so many version in adverts and I keep telling her no.

replies.author: Ok-Constant-8319
replies.body:
Same. I thought I would teach the kids a lesson a year or so ago and I let them both get some games with ads. what I always call scam games. well, man was I wrong haha. they practically play some of the games just for the ad-based games now lol. and they find it even more hilarious that it makes me a little crazy listening to the ads, so they get even more entertainment value from playing them near me when an ad plays lol.

I generally just tell them now to only get the Apple Arcade games as a lot of these types of games you can find on there, but not all.

I love the sorting game. If I had one suggestion, I'd tell whichever ai you made it with to try animating the bolts unbolting and bolting on. not 'instant' like it is now, but I think it could just have a long running animation and then multiple pieces could move at once and it would be even more 'cozy'. the 'snap' to the other bolt doesn't jive as well with the overall flow. that being said I have already played it a bunch myself and I love it. thanks for sharing!

on mine, if any issues, they both have links in there somewhere I think to GitHub, but they are both at on GitHub here:  
[https://github.com/royashbrook/craftrush](https://github.com/royashbrook/craftrush)  
[https://github.com/royashbrook/quantamari](https://github.com/royashbrook/quantamari)

replies.author: ScaleInfamous1847
replies.body:
I'm so new to the git hub thing it took ages for me to bite the bullet. I'm an old fart been programming for about 20 years and was really hesitant to use AI but I've found the more I work on it the more it's a collaborative effort - I'm enjoying steering it the way I want far more than chasing a bit I created.

Interesting future we're heading into for sure.

Funny really, when my kid was 6 I did a coding club after school with her mates had loads of them on Chromebooks with little Microbits and I wonder if all that's pointless now?

And now I'm sad 🤣

comments.body: The "again" button does not work correctly , it doesnt reset the puzzle and kinda breaks the game.

replies.author: ScaleInfamous1847
replies.body: Ooh, good spot! I'll sort that now.

comments.author: Hybridxx9018
comments.body: Kids these days really missing out on the free flash game era.

replies.author: ScaleInfamous1847
replies.body:
I've been an IT tech in a high school for nearly 21 years now - I remember when they were obsessed with Yeti Sports 🤣

Always found the best games watching what the kids were wasting time on.

comments.author: MunchyCerealGuy
comments.body: This is awesome! Really good quality and I can see you paid attention to the mobile screen adaptiveness. I'm seeing a trend of developer moms and dads making games for/with their children and it seems to be an amazing bonding activity and way of crafting for kids.
